Section 01

Introduction

This framework gives every member of the Creative Studio clear, transparent and consistent guidance on what's expected at each level, how performance is judged, and what evidence is needed to progress.

It supports role clarity, career development, quarterly performance conversations, bonus discussions, 1:1s, progression planning and promotion readiness.

Progression is based on consistent evidence that someone is already operating at the level above. A promotion confirms the level someone is already demonstrating — it isn't the starting point for developing those skills.

What the framework should help answer

  • What's expected of me in my current role?
  • What does good performance look like at my level?
  • What does the next level require?
  • What evidence do I need to show I'm ready?
  • How can my manager help me set goals and track progress?
  • How does my work support Quantum's brand, customers, marketing performance and commercial growth?

Performance vs progression

QuestionMeaning
PerformanceHow well has this person performed in their current role this quarter?
ProgressionIs this person consistently demonstrating that they're already operating at the level above?
Section 02

Alignment to Quantum brand & culture

This framework is built around Quantum's Brand & Culture framework. Our vision, mission, values, guiding principles and competencies define how the Creative Studio operates, collaborates, leads and grows.

The previous QiH job levelling framework was used only as a structural reference for level logic, consistency and progression. The new Creative Studio framework is intentionally designed to reflect Quantum's future direction, ambition and culture.

Quantum ambition

Vision

Support Quantum in becoming the world's most used digital comparison service by creating work that gives value and simplicity to users.

Mission

Connect global brands with high-intent consumers through clear, effective, trustworthy and performance-led creative work.

Goal

Contribute to the ambition of a £1 billion valuation by 2032 through creative quality, efficiency, brand strength, customer clarity and commercial impact.

Guiding principles

PrincipleCreative Studio interpretation
Performance-driven cultureResults over effort, outcomes over tasks. Creative work is judged by quality, impact and contribution — not activity alone.
Data-driven decision-makingData is our foundation, insight is our edge. Creative decisions use evidence, customer insight, testing and performance learning.
Growth-driven leadershipStanding still means moving backwards. Feedback, coaching, development, AI adoption and continuous improvement are part of how the studio works.

Quantum values

Build Together

Collaborate early, share thinking, challenge constructively and help the team succeed.

All In

Take ownership of work, outcomes, quality, feedback, deadlines and improvement.

Be Brave

Challenge weak thinking, test quickly, learn fast and take action rather than waiting for perfect conditions.

Push the Limits

Set a high bar, improve quality, raise standards and look for better ways of working.

Embrace Change

Adapt quickly, learn new tools, use AI and automation, and treat change as fuel for growth.

Quantum competencies

CompetencyFramework interpretation
Learning agilityLearns fast, applies feedback, improves continuously and embraces new tools and AI.
AccountabilityOwns outcomes, follows through, admits mistakes and acts decisively.
ResilienceMaintains focus and performance under pressure, change or ambiguity.
Problem-solvingBreaks down challenges, uses data and creativity, and moves quickly from issue to solution.
CuriosityAsks better questions, seeks insight and stays open to new ideas.

L10 (CMO) sits in executive marketing leadership above the Creative Studio. L9 is reserved for a future senior creative or brand leadership role and isn't currently scoped.

The four step-ups

Every transition above senior contributor is a step-change in role type — not just an incremental promotion. The shift each time is in what the role is accountable for.

Step-up 01
Senior Contributor → Lead

From delivering excellent work personally to helping others deliver excellent work.

Step-up 02
Lead → Head of Discipline

From leading day-to-day output to owning discipline standards, systems and capability.

Step-up 03
Head of Discipline → Head of Creative

From leading one specialism to leading the Creative Studio across disciplines.

Step-up 04
Head of Creative → Creative Director

From leading studio delivery to setting creative vision and strategic business direction.

Section 05

Job descriptions

Each job description defines the purpose, responsibilities and expectations of the role. Read them alongside the Performance Expectations Matrix, Quarterly Performance Assessment and Progression Criteria.

Performance isn't only measured by what someone delivers — it's measured by how they deliver it: through ownership, collaboration, curiosity, accountability, pace, resilience, problem-solving, data-led thinking and openness to change.

L1Graduate Designer12-month FTC / Graduate Scheme+
Discipline
Design
Working pattern
12-month FTC / Graduate Scheme
Reports to
Senior Digital Designer / Creative Lead
Progression route
Junior Digital Designer
Role purpose

The Graduate Designer supports the Creative Studio by learning the foundations of digital design, brand application, campaign delivery and creative production.

Role summary

As a Graduate Designer, you support the design team with digital assets across paid media, CRM, social, landing pages and internal creative projects. You learn how to interpret briefs, apply brand guidelines and use creative tools effectively.

Quantum behaviours expected in this role
Build TogetherWorks openly with the team, asks questions, listens to feedback and supports others where possible.
All InTakes responsibility for learning, completing tasks carefully and following through on commitments.
Be BraveTries new ideas, asks questions, learns from mistakes and applies feedback quickly.
Push the LimitsShows ambition to improve craft, quality and confidence with every brief.
Embrace ChangeAdapts to new tools, processes, feedback and priorities, including learning how AI can support creative work.
Key responsibilities
Creative design and execution
  • Create high-quality static, motion and digital assets across CRM, paid media, social, display, landing pages and other marketing channels.
  • Translate briefs, brand objectives and campaign goals into clear, effective and visually engaging creative solutions.
  • Apply strong design fundamentals including layout, typography, hierarchy, colour, composition, motion and digital craft.
Brand consistency and quality
  • Apply brand guidelines and visual identity consistently across multiple brands and channels.
  • Maintain high standards of accuracy, file quality, detail and creative polish.
  • Use feedback to improve the quality, clarity and effectiveness of design work.
Campaign, channel and performance delivery
  • Design assets for CRM, paid media, paid social, display, web and owned channels.
  • Apply channel knowledge, platform best practice, user journey understanding and performance objectives.
  • Use data, feedback and campaign learnings to improve creative output.
AI, tools and innovation
  • Use AI and creative tools appropriately to improve exploration, speed, quality, variation and workflow efficiency.
  • Review AI-assisted outputs critically to protect brand quality, originality, compliance and creative judgement.
  • Stay curious about new tools, formats, automation and performance-led creative approaches.
Collaboration and communication
  • Work closely with designers, copy/content, marketing, CRM, product and commercial stakeholders.
  • Ask clear questions, communicate progress and blockers, and present rationale appropriate to level.
  • Receive feedback constructively and apply it effectively.
Process, organisation and delivery
  • Manage files, naming conventions, version control and handovers to a high standard.
  • Deliver work accurately and to agreed timelines.
  • Identify blockers early and help improve templates, systems and ways of working.
What good looks like

A successful Graduate Designer delivers work appropriate to level, improves through feedback and builds confidence in the craft, tools, channels and processes required for the role.

They demonstrate Quantum culture through curiosity, coachability, accountability, openness to feedback and willingness to learn new tools, including AI.

Skills and experience
  • 0-1 years of relevant design or creative experience.
  • Strong design fundamentals across layout, typography, hierarchy, colour, composition and digital craft.
  • Working knowledge of Adobe Creative Suite, Figma and relevant digital design tools.
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to quality.
  • Ability to use feedback, data and insight to improve work.
  • Positive and practical approach to AI and automation as creative accelerators.
Nice to have
  • Experience in iGaming, affiliate marketing, comparison, sport, entertainment, e-commerce or performance-led industries.
  • Experience with Smartly, Bannerflow, programmatic creative or automation platforms.
  • Experience with motion, CRM, UI/UX, landing page optimisation or design systems.
Key stakeholders
  • Creative Studio team
  • Creative Director / Head of Creative where relevant
  • Marketing team
  • CRM team
  • Product team
  • Commercial stakeholders
  • Brand stakeholders
To progress to Junior Digital Designer
  • Deliver simple briefs with increasing confidence and reduced support.
  • Apply brand guidelines or tone of voice guidance accurately.
  • Take feedback well and apply it effectively.
  • Manage basic tasks and deadlines reliably.
  • Show curiosity and initiative in learning tools, channels and AI.
  • Understand how creative work supports campaigns, customer journeys and marketing goals.
  • Demonstrate the Quantum values and competencies expected at the level above.
Evidence of readiness / high performance
  • Examples of tasks or briefs delivered successfully.
  • Work showing improved quality over time.
  • Positive feedback from a manager, senior creative or stakeholder.
  • Examples of applying brand guidelines or tone of voice correctly.
  • Evidence of reliable organisation, file/document setup and delivery.
  • Examples of using AI appropriately to support learning or workflow.

Role purpose

Role summary

You support copy across email, paid social, organic social, landing pages, websites and campaign messaging while learning how copy supports brand quality and customer action.

Quantum behaviours expected in this role
Build TogetherWorks openly with the team, asks questions, listens to feedback and supports others where possible.
All InTakes responsibility for learning, completing tasks carefully and following through on commitments.
Be BraveTries new ideas, asks questions, learns from mistakes and applies feedback quickly.
Push the LimitsShows ambition to improve craft, quality and confidence with every brief.
Embrace ChangeAdapts to new tools, processes, feedback and priorities, including learning how AI can support creative work.
Key responsibilities
Brand writing and content creation
  • Write clear, engaging and on-brand copy across email, paid social, organic social, landing pages, websites, editorial content and campaign messaging.
  • Translate creative and marketing briefs into content that drives clarity, action and engagement.
  • Adapt copy to suit different brands, audiences, channels, verticals and campaign objectives.
Tone of voice and brand consistency
  • Apply tone of voice guidelines consistently across the Creative Studio brand portfolio.
  • Help maintain consistency in how brands sound across campaigns, products, landing pages, CRM and social channels.
  • Identify where copy, messaging or tone of voice feels inconsistent and suggest improvements.
Campaign, content and optimisation
  • Produce campaign copy that supports acquisition, engagement, conversion, retention and brand awareness.
  • Work with designers to ensure copy and visual design work together effectively.
  • Use data, performance insights, testing and feedback to refine copy and improve effectiveness.
AI implementation and content efficiency
  • Use AI tools appropriately for research, ideation, headline exploration, content variation, drafting, editing, summarisation and optimisation.
  • Review AI-assisted outputs critically to ensure brand fit, quality, originality, compliance and accuracy.
  • Identify where AI can support faster production, testing, localisation, repurposing or content scaling.
Content management and operations
  • Support or own content libraries, templates, frameworks, guidelines and documentation appropriate to level.
  • Maintain clear version control and accuracy across content documents and platforms.
  • Improve reusable templates, playbooks and content systems that increase consistency and efficiency.
Collaboration and communication
  • Work closely with Creative Director, designers, marketers, CRM, product and brand stakeholders.
  • Take part in creative reviews, brainstorms, feedback loops and campaign planning.
  • Present copy and content rationale clearly where needed and apply feedback constructively.

A successful Graduate Copywriter delivers work appropriate to level, improves through feedback and builds confidence in the craft, tools, channels and processes required for the role.

Role purpose

The Creative Director sets the creative vision, strategic direction and business-level creative standards for Quantum Creative Studio.

Role summary

You shape creative direction across the brand portfolio, campaigns, products, customer journeys and marketing activity. You are accountable for studio vision, standards, leadership, operating model, strategic influence, culture and future capability.

Quantum behaviours expected in this role
Build TogetherBuilds a Creative Studio that works as a strategic partner across Marketing, Product, Commercial and senior leadership.
All InTakes accountability for creative vision, standards, performance, culture and commercial contribution.
Be BraveSets bold creative direction, challenges the business constructively and creates a culture where testing, learning and decisive action are expected.
Push the LimitsContinuously raises creative output, team capability, brand quality, customer experience and commercial impact.
Embrace ChangeLeads the future direction of the studio across AI, automation, data-led creative and evolving business priorities.
Key responsibilities
Creative vision and strategy

Business and commercial leadership

Studio leadership, brand and future capability

  • Define the studio approach to AI, automation, data-led creative and future capability.
What good looks like

A successful Creative Director leads a Creative Studio that is strategically aligned, creatively ambitious, commercially effective and future-facing.

They set vision, develop creative leaders, raise standards and ensure the studio contributes to brand strength, marketing performance and business growth.

Section 07

Quarterly performance assessment

The quarterly assessment gives managers and team members a simple, consistent way to review performance based on evidence from the previous quarter.

Assessment model by level

Level rangePerformance areas
L1–L5Collaboration, Problem Solving, Ownership, Results
L6–L8Leadership, Problem Solving, Ownership, Results

Performance area definitions

Leadership

Influences peers and stakeholders, drives team success, and leads collaborative efforts.

Collaboration

Works effectively with others to support shared outcomes, communicate clearly and contribute to team success.

Problem solving

Identifies challenges and develops effective solutions.

Ownership

Takes responsibility and proactively addresses issues.

Results

Achieves goals and delivers measurable outcomes.

Rating scale

RatingMeaning
GreatExceeding expectations
GoodMeeting expectations
OK for nowLow meeting expectations / high needs improvement
Not OKNeeds improvement; performance in this area is well below expectations

Ratings should be based on evidence from the quarter — not personality, effort alone, busyness or isolated examples.

Section 08

Progression criteria

Progression criteria define what someone needs to demonstrate to move to the next level. Each progression step includes the core shift, up to three goals, evidence of readiness and manager support.

L1 → L2

Core shift

From learning and supporting simple tasks to taking ownership of smaller briefs with guidance.

Progression goals

  • Deliver simple briefs with increasing independence.
  • Show consistent application of feedback and brand standards.
  • Build confidence in one agreed development area.

Evidence of readiness

  • Consistent evidence across more than one project or moment.
  • Evidence linked to the relevant quarterly performance and capability areas.
  • Clear examples of Quantum behaviours demonstrated at the level above.
  • Manager observations, stakeholder feedback, outcomes, quality improvements or measurable impact.
What progression isn't: Progression isn't based on time served, effort alone, potential, or one isolated strong example. It's based on consistent evidence that the individual is already operating at the level above.
L2 → L3

Core shift

From owning smaller briefs with guidance to owning standard briefs independently.

Progression goals

  • Own standard briefs independently.
  • Improve creative quality and reduce rework.
  • Demonstrate independent workflow and problem-solving.

Evidence of readiness

  • Consistent evidence across more than one project or moment.
  • Evidence linked to the relevant quarterly performance and capability areas.
  • Clear examples of Quantum behaviours demonstrated at the level above.
  • Manager observations, stakeholder feedback, outcomes, quality improvements or measurable impact.
What progression isn't: Progression isn't based on time served, effort alone, potential, or one isolated strong example. It's based on consistent evidence that the individual is already operating at the level above.
L3 → L4

Core shift

From owning standard briefs independently to owning complex briefs and helping raise standards around them.

Progression goals

Evidence of readiness

  • Consistent evidence across more than one project or moment.

What progression isn't: Progression isn't based on time served, effort alone, potential, or one isolated strong example. It's based on consistent evidence that the individual is already operating at the level above.

Section 11

Bonus and performance alignment

The framework supports performance and bonus conversations by creating a consistent, evidence-led way to review what was delivered, how it was delivered and what impact it had.

Performance is judged against

  • Agreed goals.
  • The four quarterly performance areas.
  • Quality and impact of work.
  • Quantum behaviours.
  • Evidence from the quarter.

Bonus conversations are not based on

  • Effort, busyness or intentions alone.
  • Personal preference.
  • One isolated success.
  • Time served.
  • Visibility without impact.

Performance and progression are connected but not the same. A person can be performing well at their current level but not yet be demonstrating the level above.

Guiding principle: performance is assessed by the quality, consistency and impact of outcomes delivered — and by the behaviours shown in delivering them.

Section 12

Manager guidance

How to use the framework day to day — for goal setting, feedback, fair assessment and progression conversations.

How to use the framework

  • Clarify expectations at each level.
  • Set meaningful, evidence-based goals.
  • Give feedback linked to role expectations and Quantum behaviours.
  • Track evidence over time.
  • Assess quarterly performance fairly.
  • Discuss progression using evidence, not opinion.

How to assess performance fairly

Consider what was delivered, how it was delivered, quality, impact, behaviours, response to feedback and contribution to outcomes.

Don't judge performance on personality, effort alone, busyness, intentions without outcomes, isolated examples, personal preference or length of service.

Use the same framework for everyone and document evidence throughout the quarter.

How to give feedback

Use this simple structure: what happened, why it matters, what good would look like, and what to do next.

How to discuss progression

  • Ask what level the person is aiming for.
  • Review which next-level expectations are already being demonstrated.
  • Identify evidence and gaps.
  • Agree up to three goals that build next-level evidence.
  • Clarify what support the manager will provide.

Manager checklist

QuestionYes / No
Have I reviewed the person's JD and level expectations?
Have I reviewed evidence from the quarter?
Have I assessed the correct four performance areas?
Have I separated performance from progression readiness?
Have I linked feedback to evidence?
Have I considered Quantum behaviours?
Have I agreed up to three clear goals?
Have I documented manager support and next actions?

Plain-English principle: Where are you now? Where are you trying to get to? What evidence do we need to show you're ready?
